name: Slow Cooker Crack Chicken Bowls
intro_html: Crack chicken earned its nickname honestly, because the creamy, cheesy, bacon-flecked flavor is genuinely hard to stop eating. This bowl packs {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost), served over tender potatoes. It runs a touch pricier than the others, but 14 servings from one pot still makes it a bargain against takeout.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3450 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 2/3 cup (140 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 8 lb: ~$16.96. Buy 8 lbs: $17.84.
Ranch Seasoning Mix, 6 1/2 tbsp: ~$0.72. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 1oz packets.

Batch total: about $25.38 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.81 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $31.00 across 14 servings, roughly $2.21 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $1.18 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $32.18. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Bacon is the priciest bit here, so use it as a topping, not a base, and a little goes a long way for that smoky hit.
Skip the packet and mix your own ranch seasoning from dried herbs, which is cheaper and lets you dial back the salt.
The lower-fat cream cheese and a modest handful of cheddar keep this rich without wrecking the budget, so buy the store-brand blocks.
make_it: Add the chicken, cream cheese, ranch seasoning, and chicken broth to the slow cooker.
Nestle the cut potatoes around the chicken so they cook in the creamy broth.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the potatoes are tender and the chicken shreds.
Cook and crumble the bacon while everything finishes.
Shred the chicken, stir in the shredded cheddar until melted, then top with the crumbled bacon and serve.
portion_html: Each serving carries {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories, indulgent tasting but still protein-forward.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Hungry Hobby, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Sometimes the comfort-food bowl is exactly what gets you through a long week, and this one earns it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
